eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Four
subtitle: Lesson 40 · Grouping and Aggregating

eyebrow: Subtotals, plus a grand total, in one query
code:
SELECT Color, Size, SUM(ListPrice) AS TotalListPrice,
       COUNT(*) AS ProductCount
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size);
caption: Every (Color, Size) row, PLUS a subtotal per Color, PLUS one grand total.

eyebrow: Right to left, in the order you give it
code:
-- ROLLUP (Color, Size): rolls up Size first, then Color
-- ROLLUP (Size, Color): rolls up the other way instead
caption: ROLLUP doesn't know your data's hierarchy — it just follows column order.

eyebrow: The problem: two kinds of NULL
code:
-- Some products have a genuinely NULL Color in the data.
-- ROLLUP ALSO inserts NULL to mean "this is a subtotal."
-- How do you tell them apart?
caption: A NULL alone can't tell you which one you're looking at.

code:
SELECT Color, Size, SUM(ListPrice) AS TotalListPrice,
       GROUPING(Color) AS IsColorSubtotal,
       GROUPING(Size) AS IsSizeSubtotal
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size);
caption: 1 = this NULL came from ROLLUP. 0 = a real group value.

subtitle: Every combination, not just a hierarchy.
